paragraphs: Oral and maxillofacial surgery work starts with history, intraoral examination, occlusion, and imaging, producing indications, alternatives, anesthesia level, surgical approach, instruments, emergency plans, and follow-up outputs. The 1st verification point requires putting the patient, clinical records, imaging, medications, anesthesia, surgical operations, nursing handover, and practice authorization in the same chain of responsibility; any insufficient information should stop, undergo human review, or escalate, and process speed must not replace patient safety.

Core process: Check symptoms, oral and maxillofacial imaging, and systemic risks; identify impacted teeth, infection, tumors, or trauma; determine the surgical scope, anesthesia, and consultation plan; explain alternatives, risks, and recovery.
Works in hospitals, dental specialty clinics, or surgical centers, and may take on acute maxillofacial trauma and infection.
Common tools and systems: dental imaging, CT, oral surgery instruments, anesthesia monitoring equipment, and electronic medical records.

Compared with adjacent roles, this occupation requires a dental professional degree, surgical residency training, and local licensure and surgical authority; it differs from general dentistry, orthodontics, or dental technicians.
Qualified delivery must demonstrate: imaging diagnosis, surgical plans, anesthesia assessment, informed consent, surgery, and follow-up records.
U.S. occupational scope and Chinese position titles or credentials need not correspond one-to-one; local requirements are verified by region and employer.

General dentists mainly perform routine oral diagnosis and treatment; this occupation focuses more on requiring a dental professional degree, surgical residency training, and local licensure and surgical authority; it differs from general dentistry, orthodontics, or dental technicians.
Orthodontists focus on dentofacial correction, with different occupational tasks and training.
Prosthodontists lean toward dentition and oral prosthetics; look at the final output rather than similar titles.
Difference between general dentists and this occupation: maxillofacial surgery requires additional surgical training.
Choosing general dentistry suits those who prefer general dental practice.
Explorer
Use fictional samples to learn about history and imaging.
Incumbent
Check imaging diagnosis, surgical plans, anesthesia assessment, informed consent, surgery, and follow-up records, and observe authorization.
Crew lead
Check tool use, clinical review, and the responsibility for surgery, anesthesia, and anomaly escalation; document organization does not change medical authority.
Career changer
Compare the education, training, and authority of the target dental, pediatric surgery, or technical position; oral and maxillofacial surgical authority cannot be transferred.

Insufficient evidence: a nationwide comparable median for Chinese oral and maxillofacial surgeons was not obtained. In 2025, pre-tax annual averages for health and social work were 146,266 yuan for urban non-private and 75,631 yuan for private, which is only a broad medical employer industry, includes other clinical and social work positions and is not this occupation's wage or an individual range; excludes self-employed individuals and freelancers and owner-operated clinic profits, and does not apply to instrument manufacturing or sales.

BLS lists a doctoral or professional degree and internship/residency training; U.S. dental licensure, oral and maxillofacial surgery training, and anesthesia and surgical authority are verified by state and organization, and Chinese physician/dental qualifications require separate verification.; Real duties depend on local rules and employer authorization, and changing roles requires training for the target position.
Training and authorization

Problem statement: fictional K01 planned site is the left side, the imaging label says right side, and informed consent still says left; for L01 the three sites agree, but the anesthesia assessment and authorized review signature are blank, and a newcomer wants to start surgery as scheduled. Paper rule: identifiers and site must agree and complete documents must be reviewed by an authorized person. List the hold and transfer questions, and do not select a surgical approach or anesthetic agent.
Fictional surgical document problem statement

Reference: K's site conflict is held pending verification of the original plan, imaging, and consent, and the input is kept without changing the side; L is marked incomplete for the missing assessment and signature and handed to the authorized physician and team, and is not released based on the appointment. Submit a two-line verification table: fictional identifiers, the three sites, missing assessment and signature items, questions to verify, transfer, and simulated review; corrections keep the original record, and no indication or surgery is judged.
Hold and transfer reference

Seven days: Day 1 copy the K/L inputs, rules, and boundaries; Days 2—3 build the two-line table verifying plan, imaging, consent, and assessment signature; Days 4—5 find the wrong side and missing items and write the hold and transfer; Days 6—7 submit the two tables, unresolved questions, and the correction trail. Keep the four risks of airway, infection, nerve injury, and bleeding, and do not start surgery or arrange real surgery or anesthesia.

career_risk_cards.heading: Main risks for oral and maxillofacial surgeons

risks.mitigation: Preoperative assessment and an emergency team on standby.
risks.scenario: Maxillofacial swelling or inadequate anesthesia assessment.
risks.title: Airway risk

risks.affected_roles: Oral and maxillofacial surgery teams involved in infection spread assessment, surgery, and follow-up
risks.consequence: Infection progression may affect patient safety and increase the emergency handling burden.
risks.mitigation: Emergency identification and hospital transfer consultation.
risks.scenario: Deep maxillofacial infection is treated late.
risks.title: Infection spread

risks.affected_roles: Oral and maxillofacial surgery teams involved in nerve injury assessment, surgery, and follow-up
risks.consequence: Paresthesia or functional impairment may occur.
risks.scenario: Insufficient verification of surgical scope and imaging.
risks.title: Nerve injury

risks.affected_roles: Oral and maxillofacial surgery teams involved in bleeding assessment, surgery, and follow-up
risks.consequence: Bleeding may occur and affect surgical safety.
risks.scenario: Coagulation or vascular risk is not assessed.
risks.title: Bleeding

risks.affected_roles: Oral and maxillofacial surgery teams involved in wrong-site assessment, surgery, and follow-up
risks.consequence: May operate on the wrong tooth or site.
risks.mitigation: Triple verification of patient, imaging, and site.
risks.title: Wrong-site surgery

risks.affected_roles: Oral and maxillofacial surgery teams involved in missed follow-up assessment, surgery, and follow-up
risks.consequence: May delay identification of postoperative bleeding, infection, or other complications.
risks.scenario: Infection or bleeding is not reviewed in time.
risks.title: Missed postoperative follow-up
